title: Manav Suthar's Ten-Wicket Masterclass Powers India to 165-Run Victory Over Sri Lanka in Galle
excerpt: The 24-year-old left-arm spinner claimed six wickets in the second innings as India bowled out Sri Lanka for 206, grabbing a 1-0 series lead in India's 600th Test.
body:
• Manav Suthar took 6-55 in the second innings and 10 wickets in the match as India won the first Test against Sri Lanka by 165 runs in Galle
  • Sri Lanka were bowled out for 206 chasing 372, with Sonal Dinusha (84) and captain Dhananjaya de Silva (59) mounting brief resistance
  • Rishabh Pant became the first Indian batter and fourth overall to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket during India's second innings
  • The victory in India's 600th Test gives them a 1-0 lead ahead of the second and final Test in Colombo on Sunday

Suthar Spins India to Comprehensive Win

Left-arm spinner Manav Suthar claimed six second-innings wickets in a devastating display of spin bowling to hand India a 165-run victory in the opening Test against Sri Lanka in Galle on Wednesday, minutes before rain arrived at the coastal ground.

https://x.com/BCCI/status/2089988955005677866

Playing just his second Test, the 24-year-old finished with match figures of 10 wickets — four in the first innings and six for 55 in the second — as India bowled out Sri Lanka for 206 in the post-lunch session on the final day. It was a commanding performance that announced Suthar as a genuine long-term prospect in India's spin arsenal.

"Suthar missed a hat-trick but sent down a three-wicket over to send Sri Lanka hurtling towards defeat."

— Reuters

Sri Lanka's Resistance Falls Short

Set a victory target of 372, Sri Lanka resumed day five on 84-4 and needed to bat out of their skin, possibly with some help from the weather, to save the match. For a while, they found both.

Captain Dhananjaya de Silva and Sonal Dinusha struck fighting fifties and defied India with a 95-run stand for the fifth wicket. Dinusha, who had scored a maiden Test hundred in the first innings, looked set for another significant contribution. De Silva played fluently until he fluffed a sweep shot against Ravindra Jadeja, and from that moment, India's victory was a matter of time.

Suthar tore through the lower order with ruthless efficiency. He denied Dinusha his second hundred of the match and clean bowled Prabath Jayasuriya with the next delivery. The left-armer then dismissed Lahiru Kumara with the final ball of that over and sent back Keshara Nuwantha in the same fashion to seal the result.

Pant Makes History

Earlier in the match, Rishabh Pant produced a typically audacious knock in India's second innings. The wicketkeeper-batter struck eight fours and two sixes, scoring at nearly a run-a-ball, and became the first Indian and fourth player overall to reach 100 sixes in Test cricket.

After being struck on the helmet by a Lahiru Kumara bouncer, Pant pulled the next delivery for four — a moment that captured his fearless approach. He was eventually caught behind off Kumara attempting his trademark falling-away pull shot.

India's first-innings 462 had laid the foundation, with KL Rahul contributing a composed 82. Jadeja chipped in with three wickets in both innings, while Mohammed Siraj provided pace support at crucial moments.

WTC Final Charge and What's Next

The victory is India's latest step in their push toward the World Test Championship Final. Under stand-in captain Shubman Gill — who produced a stunning diving catch to dismiss Kamindu Mendis in the first innings — India displayed the kind of clinical, multi-faceted cricket that has defined their Test dominance on the subcontinent.

The win also came in India's 600th Test match, a milestone the team marked in emphatic fashion. Dinesh Chandimal's injury during the match, which forced Sri Lanka to use concussion substitute Pasindu Sooriyabandara in his maiden Test, added to the hosts' woes.

The second and final Test begins in Colombo on Sunday, where India will look to clinch the series while continuing to build their WTC points tally.
